answer: A concrete Sybil-resistance mechanism in an AI-agent economy is slashable staking: each identity must bond tokens that stay locked across multiple epochs. An attacker spawning many fakes multiplies capital at risk, because peers can challenge coordinated abuse and burn the stake. The cost grows linearly with fake identities while gains do not, rendering large attacks uneconomic. It is like spotting a comet that paints a unique pigment trail over marble—duplicates are obvious and expensive to forge.
